findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows attacker-controlled negative offsets
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result explicitly allows negative slicing (start_offset = cursor.offset when offset < 0) when enable_advanced_features is true. Cursor values come from the user-controlled cursor query param via Cursor.from_string, so any caller can supply a negative offset. The comment claims Django ORM properly handles negative slicing, which is false — Django raises ValueError/AssertionError for negative slicing. Consequence is at minimum a 500/DoS on crafted cursors and unexpected queryset slicing semantics exposed to API users.

findings.title: Audit-log endpoint exposes vulnerable advanced paginator via query param
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:82 the endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True when ?optimized_pagination=true and requester has global access. This exposes the negative-offset code path in paginator.py to remote authenticated users. There is no test or need for this path, and permission gating does not mitigate the crash/incorrect-pagination behavior because the cursor offset itself remains attacker-controlled.

findings.title: BasePaginator has inconsistent negative-offset handling
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is still passed to queryset[start_offset:stop], which Django rejects, while the later length check uses the original offset (len(results) == offset + limit + extra). Consequence is crashes on crafted prev cursors and wrong prev-page trimming logic.

findings.title: SET to ZSET type change breaks existing Redis keys
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 ingestion changed from SADD to ZADD and from SSCAN to ZSCAN, and src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua changed SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN for keys span-buf:s:*. Existing production keys with 3600s TTL are SET type. ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN against a SET raises WRONGTYPE, so after deploy every write/read to a live segment fails until keys expire. Consequence is ingestion errors, lost segments, and consumer stalls with no migration or versioning.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE sums timestamps
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 and :53 ZUNIONSTORE is called as zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) with default AGGREGATE SUM. Members are span payloads scored by end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload exists in both inputs (retries, overlapping batches, re-joins), the score becomes sum of timestamps instead of the timestamp, corrupting ordering and the ZPOPMIN eviction that is supposed to drop oldest spans. Should be AGGREGATE MAX/MIN. Consequence is wrong eviction and inflated scores that pin duplicates.

findings.title: Hard KeyError on end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 process_batch does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with direct indexing. Any malformed, old-schema, or Relay message missing that field raises KeyError inside the Arroyo processing step, failing the whole batch and causing retries/stalls. Previously the field was not required. Consequence is a single bad Kafka message can block progress; should use .get with fallback/validation and dead-letter handling.

findings.title: Hardcoded 1000 cap diverges from max_segment_spans config
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 eviction uses hardcoded if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin, while SpansBuffer defines max_segment_spans=1001 and the old Python-side span-count guard and metric segment_span_count_exceeded were deleted in src/sentry/spans/buffer.py. Consequence is operators cannot tune the cap, the metric/log disappears, and Python/ Lua limits disagree, silently truncating segments without visibility.

findings.title: Redirect-depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep traces
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 the redirect-chain loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces/segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will no longer resolve to a single set_key, so spans that should be joined stay in separate Redis sets and flush as duplicate/split segments. Consequence is data fragmentation and duplicate segments for very deep traces with no benefit shown.
